sections.content: Most people think you need deep pockets to get started in real estate. The truth? Wholesaling lets you earn real money without buying a single property. You act as the middleman — finding distressed properties, getting them under contract, and then selling that contract to a cash buyer for a profit. No mortgage, no renovation costs, no landlord headaches. If you're brand new to this strategy, start with our [Wholesale Real Estate for Beginners: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesale-real-estate-beginners-guide) to understand the full picture before diving in.
What Does 'Wholesaling with No Money' Actually Mean?

When people ask how to wholesale real estate with no money, they usually mean one of two things: they have no savings to invest, or they don't want to risk their own capital. The good news is that both situations are fine for wholesaling. In a typical deal, you find a motivated seller willing to accept below-market value for a quick sale. You sign a purchase agreement with them, then assign that contract to an end buyer — usually a cash investor or house flipper — for a fee. That fee, called an assignment fee, is your profit. It typically ranges from $5,000 to $20,000 per deal, though some wholesalers earn $30,000 or more on bigger transactions.
'Wholesaling is the closest thing to a real estate business you can start with a phone, some hustle, and zero dollars in the bank.' — Common wisdom among experienced real estate investors
Step-by-Step: How to Wholesale Real Estate with No Money
Step 1: Learn the Basics and Know Your Numbers

Before you approach a single seller, you need to understand how to evaluate a deal. The most important number is the After Repair Value (ARV) — what the property will be worth after renovations. From there, you back out the rehab costs and your buyer's profit margin. A simple formula most wholesalers use is: Maximum Allowable Offer (MAO) = ARV × 70% − Estimated Repairs. For example, if a home has an ARV of $200,000 and needs $30,000 in repairs, your MAO would be $110,000. That's the most you can offer the seller and still leave room for your fee and your buyer's profit. Use the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) at AIWholesail to run these numbers quickly before making any offers.
Step 2: Find Motivated Sellers

Finding motivated sellers is the heart of wholesaling — and it costs little to nothing when you start smart. Motivated sellers are people who need to sell fast due to life circumstances: divorce, job loss, inherited properties, tax liens, or homes in serious disrepair. Here are the most effective zero-cost methods to find them:

items: Drive for Dollars: Drive through neighborhoods and look for vacant, overgrown, or run-down properties. Note the address and search for the owner's contact info using free tools or your county's public records.
Bandit Signs: Simple 'We Buy Houses' signs placed in high-traffic areas cost a few dollars each and can generate consistent inbound leads.
Free Online Listings: Search Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and Zillow for 'as-is' or 'cash only' listings — these are often motivated sellers already.
Probate and Tax Delinquent Lists: Most counties publish these records for free. Property owners on these lists are often highly motivated to sell quickly.
Word of Mouth and Networking: Tell everyone you know that you buy houses. Attend local real estate investor meetups and connect with agents who work with distressed sellers.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Focus your search on one or two zip codes when you're starting out. Becoming an expert in a small area helps you estimate ARVs faster and build relationships with local cash buyers who will buy your deals repeatedly. Active wholesale markets like [Atlanta, GA](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Houston, TX](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/houston-tx), and [Phoenix, AZ](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az) have strong cash buyer pools that make closing deals much easier for beginners.
Step 3: Make Offers and Get a Property Under Contract

Once you find a motivated seller, your goal is to agree on a price and sign a purchase agreement. This contract gives you the legal right to buy the property — or, more importantly, to assign that right to another buyer. You don't need to have the money to close; you just need the contract. Many states allow you to use a standard real estate purchase contract with an 'and/or assigns' clause added to the buyer's name. This single phrase is what makes assignment possible. Check out this guide on [How to Get a Wholesale Real Estate Contract (Free Template)](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/wholesale-real-estate-contract-template) to download a ready-to-use version and understand exactly what needs to be in your agreement.
Step 4: Build Your Cash Buyer List

Your cash buyers are the investors who will purchase the contract from you and actually close on the property. Building this list should happen in parallel with your seller outreach — not after. Attend local real estate investment association (REIA) meetings, post in real estate Facebook groups, and connect with investors on BiggerPockets. You can also pull public records from recent cash sales in your target area and reach out directly to those buyers. When you have a deal under contract, email your entire list with the property address, your asking price, ARV, estimated repairs, and photos. Investors move fast, so a good deal often sells within 24 to 72 hours.
Step 5: Assign the Contract and Collect Your Fee

When a cash buyer agrees to your price, you sign an Assignment of Contract document that transfers your purchase rights to them for your agreed-upon fee. For example, if you have the property under contract at $110,000 and your buyer agrees to pay $125,000, your assignment fee is $15,000. The title company or closing attorney handles the transaction, and your fee is paid out at closing. From start to finish, a wholesale deal can take anywhere from two weeks to 60 days depending on the market and title process. Read more about timelines in [How Long Does a Wholesale Real Estate Deal Take?](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/how-long-wholesale-deal-takes)
Common Mistakes Beginners Make (And How to Avoid Them)

items: Overestimating ARV: Always pull at least three comparable sales (comps) within a half-mile radius and from the last 90 days. Inflated ARVs kill deals and damage your reputation with buyers.
Underestimating Repairs: When in doubt, add a 10-15% buffer to any repair estimate. Experienced investors know surprises always happen.
Not Having a Buyer First: Ideally, you should already know who your likely buyers are before you lock up a property. Running deals the other way around wastes everyone's time.
Skipping Due Diligence on Title: Always do a basic title search before assigning a contract. Hidden liens or ownership disputes can blow up a closing fast.
Trying to Do Too Much at Once: Focus on one market, one strategy, and one deal at a time until you've closed your first check.

sections.content: Is Wholesaling Better Than Flipping for Beginners?

Wholesaling and flipping are both legitimate ways to profit from real estate, but they serve different goals and require different resources. Wholesaling is faster, lower risk, and requires no capital — making it the ideal entry point for most beginners. Flipping offers higher potential profits but requires funding, construction management skills, and a higher risk tolerance. If you're not sure which path fits your situation, read our breakdown of [Wholesale Real Estate vs Flipping: Which Strategy Is Right?](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/wholesale-real-estate-vs-flipping) to make a confident decision. You can also explore our broader [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide to understand all your options before committing.
How Much Can You Realistically Make?

First-time wholesalers often close their first deal within 30 to 90 days of serious effort. Assignment fees on a starter deal might be $3,000 to $8,000 — modest, but real money with zero capital at risk. As you build your buyer list and sharpen your skills, $10,000 to $20,000 per deal becomes very achievable. Some experienced wholesalers do 2 to 4 deals per month and earn six figures annually. The key variable isn't luck — it's the consistency of your lead generation and the strength of your buyer network. For a deeper dive into getting started, the [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through every foundational concept in plain language.

Pro Tip: Track every lead, every offer, and every follow-up in a simple spreadsheet or free CRM. Most deals don't close on the first contact — studies show it takes 5 to 8 touchpoints with a motivated seller before they agree to a price. Consistent follow-up is what separates beginners who close deals from those who don't.
